How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a little bit hard, since a lot of people wanted someone from the state to vouch for us

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It’s really nice and i Think it gives more freedom when it comes to going out. Also i Think the quality of the apartments are better than the student dormitories. But no matter where you live in Ankara it takes 30-60 minutes to come to campus (Beytepe)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We just went to the student affairs office and gave our passports then they fixed everything for us and gave us a student ID number, afterwards we got a paper and had to go to another office and apply for our student ID card (on campus). Our Erasmus coordinator helped us pick out classes so we didn’t have to do anything online on the schools website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Everyone was very helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, our Erasmus coordinator helped us with everything

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just use your coordinator as much as possible and don’t be afraid to say no to some classes if you don’t want them, even though they think you should do it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Too hard for us, we don’t speak fluent Turkish

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Too many courses (7-8), which was held on academic Turkish. Our level at the time was A2-B1, not enough at all

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We were just supposed to sit and listen and take notes by hand. Hard to keep up when you don’t engage in the class

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: Easy, as i know the Turkish culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak turkish, dont be afraid

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Most people Didnt really speak English

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Over all turkish people are very kind

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Find an apartment close to the city center (kizilay)
2. Go to all the events, even though you feel like you dont want to (and socialise with the Erasmus students) 
3. Eat all the great food

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure that you speak turkish at a certain level. If not, choose another place

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being forced to speak turkish

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier
